extraction.name: TextVQA
extraction.description: A dataset containing questions on images that require reasoning about text to answer.
extraction.creator: Amanpreet Singh, Vivek Natarajan, Meet Shah, Yu Jiang, Xinlei Chen, Dhruv Batra, Devi Parikh, Marcus Rohrbach
extraction.publisher: Facebook AI Research, Georgia Institute of Technology
extraction.rai:dataCollection: A three-stage pipeline for crowd-sourcing data: identifying images with text, collecting 1-2 questions per image, and collecting 10 answers per question.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Filtering out images that did not contain text and noisy data from annotators. Removing questions where a majority of workers marked flags indicating poor quality.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotators were shown an image and asked to provide a question requiring reading text. A second question was then collected. Finally, 10 answers were collected per question with specific instructions and flags to ensure quality.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Analysis of annotator agreement on the most common answers.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Aiding visually impaired users by endowing VQA models with the ability to read text in images.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset does not have significant biases with respect to images and questions.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The OCR model used fails at detecting text that is rotated, unstructured, or partially occluded.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, validation, and testing of VQA models.

name.evidence: First, we introduce a new “TextVQA” dataset to facilitate progress on this important problem.

description.evidence: TextVQA contains 45,336 questions on 28,408 images that require reasoning about text to answer.

creator.evidence: Amanpreet Singh1, Vivek Natarajan, Meet Shah1, Yu Jiang1, Xinlei Chen1, Dhruv Batra1,2, Devi Parikh1,2, Marcus Rohrbach1

rai:dataCollection.evidence: We set up a three stage pipeline for crowd-sourcing our data. In the first stage, annotators were asked to identify images that did not contain text... In the second stage, we collect 1-2 questions for each image... we collect 10 answers for each question.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: We set up a three stage pipeline for crowd-sourcing our data.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: We use Open Images v3 dataset [27] as the source of our images.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: In the first stage, annotators were asked to identify images that did not contain text (using a forced-choice “yes”/“no” flag). Filtering those (and noisy data from annotators) out resulted in 28,408 images... We remove the questions where a majority of workers marked any of these flags.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: For the first question, we show annotators an image and ask them to provide a question which requires reading the text in the image to answer... To collect a second question that is different from the first, we show annotators the first question and ask them to come up with a question... we collect 10 answers for each question.

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: All 10 annotators agree on the most common answer for 22.8% questions, while 3 or more annotators agree on most common answer for 97.9% questions.

rai:annotationsPerItem.evidence: Following VQA [3, 10] and VizWiz [13] datasets, we collect 10 answers for each question.

rai:annotatorDemographics.evidence: It contains 45,336 questions asked by (sighted) humans on 28,408 images

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: We run a state-of-the-art OCR model Rosetta [6] on these images and compute the average number of OCR boxes in a category.

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: We explore a specific skill in Visual Question Answering that is important for the applications involving aiding visually impaired users – answering questions about everyday images that involve reading and reasoning about text in these images.

rai:dataBiases.evidence: Question only (Q) and Image only (I) baseline get 8.09% and 6.29% validation accuracies, respectively, which shows that the dataset does not have significant biases w.r.t. images and questions.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: Our OCR model, while mature, still fails at detecting text that is rotated, a bit unstructured (e.g., a scribble) or partially occluded.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: We divide TextVQA into train, validation and test splits with size 34,602, 5,000, and 5,734, respectively.
